# Real Markdown excerpts

`markdown-real.json` contains minimal, manually reviewed excerpts from local assistant transcripts. It does not contain raw events, source paths, provider metadata, user turns, timestamps, or correlation IDs.

- The path, approximation, PromQL, Python regex, and literal ellipsis cases are slices of actual thinking text. They omit enclosing tool or command text. Replacements generalize local paths, node and interface labels, private field names, and source positions; the relevant delimiters and escapes are retained.
- The strike and escaped-parenthesis cases are the interiors of syntax examples quoted as code in real replies. The corpus renders the example itself, not its surrounding code span. The inline and display math excerpts are actual formulas from reply prose, including a Chinese `\text` argument and escaped text underscores.
- The multi-chunk excerpts use boundaries from recorded server `text_delta` events. Cropping may shorten the first or last delta. Redactions in these excerpts are length-preserving across delta boundaries; the cuts are not generated by a re-chunker. Single-chunk samples do not claim to retain network delta boundaries.

To add an excerpt, select the smallest useful span and keep raw transcripts and redaction maps local. Preserve delimiters, escapes, whitespace and, when available, recorded delta boundaries. Replace private words, paths, and measurements with generic equivalents before writing the fixture. Review every decoded chunk, its concatenated text, and all JSON keys. The test rejects unknown keys, aliases, paths, words and numbers before it renders anything; additions to the allowlists require the same privacy review. Do not include original values or source locators in tests, docs, or commit messages.
